notes: Resolves a battle presentation trigger: either announces the encounter, visits unstunned living party units, or activates and tears down a selected battle object based on a bounded random test.

Correct party and unit layouts raise structural similarity to 85.58 percent, but stack layout, branch shaping, loop allocation, and call scheduling remain broad. It did not meet the bounded-search or permanent-residual gate.

2026-08-27: bounded search closed differing_halfwords from 116 to 1 (wrong_instructions 33 to 2). Three source-level fixes did the work: (1) unit_ids widened from u16 to s16 (cast to u16* only at the BattleParty_ListLivingUnits call site) so both party-index reads compile to ldrsh instead of ldrh, matching the reference's signed-extend addressing; (2) the living-unit loop condition rewritten from `index >= 0` to `index != -1`, which makes the compiler synthesize the loop bound via movs #1/negs (compare against -1) instead of cmp/blt-bge, matching the reference's loop-footer shape; (3) scene's raw pointer address rewritten as `presentation_addr - 140` (arithmetic from a u8 * holding 0x03001f00) instead of the independent literal 0x03001e74, which makes the compiler reuse the already-loaded 0x03001f00 register via `subs r3,#140` instead of emitting a second literal-pool load -- this alone recovered the full 8-byte size gap and collapsed most of the remaining diff. The encounter_mode==2/party-loop branch was also restructured as a `party_mode = completed; if (cond) party_mode = 1; if (!party_mode) ... else ...` two-statement flag pattern (rather than a direct nested if/else) to reproduce the reference's default-value-then-conditional-override branch shape (movs/beq/movs/cmp/bne) instead of a single collapsed bne -- this matched the branch senses and block order exactly.

Remaining single differing halfword (wrong_instructions=2, both counting the same spot): candidate emits `movs r2, #0` where the reference emits `adds r2, r7, #0` (copying the already-live completed==0 value from r7) to seed party_mode's default before the encounter_mode compare. Both are 2-byte, flag-setting, functionally identical zero-into-r2 encodings -- pure register-CSE opcode choice, not a control-flow or data difference. Tried and rejected (no effect, or regressed structure/size): `party_mode = completed` vs `= 0` (identical output either way -- proves the compiler constant-propagates completed to 0 before this point regardless of aliasing to the variable); `party_mode = completed + 0` (still folds to a fresh immediate); hoisting party_mode's declaration/init to function scope before the outer if (changed register allocation wholesale, regressed to candidate=260, wrong_instructions=58); u32 vs s32 type for party_mode (no effect); swapping completed/party_mode declaration order (no effect); ternary `party_mode = (encounter_mode==2) ? completed : 1` and plain if/else `party_mode = completed; else party_mode = 1;` in place of the default+override form (both collapse the compiler back to a single direct branch, losing the whole flag-materialize shape and regressing size to 244). This looks like a genuine postreload-CSE/register-allocator threshold difference between our toolchain build and whatever produced the ROM, not reachable by further legitimate C restructuring without forcing register assignment (prohibited by CONTRIBUTING.md).
